description: Dependency-free .NET 8 APIs for encoding, buffers, cryptography, timing, reflection, platform inspection, and managed-memory diagnostics.
executionSupportMessage: Compatible with the built-in .NET 10 C# runner; authored against .NET 8.

actionDescriptions.Add: Adds a value, item, header, or contribution to an existing object.
actionDescriptions.Allocate: Obtains reusable memory or another finite runtime resource for temporary work.
actionDescriptions.Compare: Compares values and reports their ordering or equality relationship.
actionDescriptions.Convert: Changes a value into another representation or data type.
actionDescriptions.Create: Constructs a new object, resource, or language structure.
actionDescriptions.Decode: Converts an encoded representation back into its original form.
actionDescriptions.Encode: Converts data into a representation suitable for storage or transport.
actionDescriptions.Enumerate: Traverses a sequence of values or members one item at a time.
actionDescriptions.Get: Retrieves information without intentionally changing the source.
actionDescriptions.Hash: Calculates a fixed-size digest from input data.
actionDescriptions.Inspect: Examines runtime metadata, state, or structure.
actionDescriptions.Parse: Interprets text or bytes as a structured value.
actionDescriptions.Protect: Applies a security-sensitive transformation or comparison.
actionDescriptions.Release: Returns or frees a resource previously acquired by the program.
actionDescriptions.Slice: Creates a bounded view over part of an existing value or memory region.
actionDescriptions.Test: Evaluates a condition and returns whether it is satisfied.

objectDescriptions.Assembly: An Assembly represents a deployed .NET code and metadata unit containing modules, types, resources, and identity information.
objectDescriptions.Data: Data is an ordered byte sequence whose representation and interpretation are defined by the producing application or protocol.
objectDescriptions.Elapsed time: Elapsed time is a duration calculated from a monotonic high-resolution timer rather than the wall clock.
objectDescriptions.Elapsed timer: An elapsed timer records monotonic timestamps for performance measurement and duration tracking.
objectDescriptions.Enum: An enum is a value type whose named constants represent a closed set of integral values.
objectDescriptions.Hexadecimal: Hexadecimal is a base-16 text representation that uses two characters per byte.
objectDescriptions.Managed allocation: A managed allocation reserves garbage-collected heap storage for a new object, array, string, or runtime structure.
objectDescriptions.Memory: Memory<T> is a heap-storable view over a contiguous region of typed elements.
objectDescriptions.Message: A message is the byte sequence whose integrity and authenticity are being protected or verified.
objectDescriptions.Method metadata: MethodInfo describes a runtime method's name, signature, declaring type, attributes, and invocation behavior.
objectDescriptions.Operating system: The operating system is the platform hosting the current .NET process.
objectDescriptions.Pooled buffer: A pooled buffer is a reusable array temporarily leased from an ArrayPool<T> to reduce allocation pressure.
objectDescriptions.Primitive bytes: Primitive bytes are the machine representation of a numeric, Boolean, character, or related built-in value.
objectDescriptions.Property metadata: PropertyInfo describes a runtime property's type, accessors, declaring type, index parameters, and attributes.
objectDescriptions.Runtime object: A runtime object is an instance whose concrete Type may have been selected dynamically rather than through a compile-time constructor expression.
objectDescriptions.Runtime type: A System.Type describes a .NET type's identity, members, inheritance, generic shape, and runtime metadata.
objectDescriptions.Secret data: Secret data includes keys, authentication tags, tokens, and other bytes whose disclosure or comparison behavior affects security.
objectDescriptions.Secure random data: Secure random data is produced by a cryptographically strong operating-system random source suitable for security-sensitive values.
objectDescriptions.Secure random number: A secure random number is sampled without predictable state or range bias for security-sensitive selection.
objectDescriptions.Text buffer: A StringBuilder is a mutable buffer optimized for incrementally constructing text.
objectDescriptions.UTF-8 text: UTF-8 is a variable-width Unicode encoding compatible with ASCII for its first 128 code points.

commands.name: StringBuilder.Append
commands.description: Append text or a value to a mutable character buffer.
commands.definition: Adds the text representation of a value to the end of a StringBuilder and returns the same builder for fluent chaining.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value or text to append.

examples.title: Build a status line incrementally
examples.explanation: Each Append mutates and returns the same buffer, avoiding a chain of temporary strings.

commands.name: StringBuilder.AppendLine
commands.description: Append text followed by a line terminator.
commands.definition: Adds text and the current environment's line terminator to a StringBuilder, returning the same builder.

examples.title: Build a multiline report
examples.explanation: AppendLine uses the current platform's line ending for every report row.

commands.name: Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes
commands.description: Encode Unicode text as UTF-8 bytes.
commands.definition: Converts UTF-16 .NET characters into the corresponding UTF-8 byte sequence. Invalid surrogate input is handled by the encoding's configured fallback.

examples.title: Inspect a UTF-8 representation
examples.code:
var bytes = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("turtle 🐢");
Console.WriteLine(Convert.ToHexString(bytes));
examples.explanation: ASCII characters occupy one byte each while the turtle emoji uses a multibyte UTF-8 sequence.

commands.name: Encoding.UTF8.GetString
commands.description: Decode UTF-8 bytes into a .NET string.
commands.definition: Interprets the supplied bytes as UTF-8 and returns UTF-16 .NET text. Invalid byte sequences use the encoding's configured fallback behavior.

examples.title: Restore UTF-8 text
examples.code:
var bytes = Convert.FromHexString("48797065727368656C6C");
Console.WriteLine(Encoding.UTF8.GetString(bytes));
examples.explanation: The hexadecimal bytes decode to the original Hypershell text.

commands.name: Convert.ToHexString
commands.description: Encode bytes as uppercase hexadecimal text.
commands.definition: Converts each byte to two hexadecimal characters and concatenates the result without separators.

examples.title: Display a compact byte signature
examples.explanation: Every hash byte becomes two uppercase hexadecimal characters.

commands.name: Convert.FromHexString
commands.description: Decode hexadecimal text into bytes.
commands.definition: Converts pairs of hexadecimal characters into their byte values. Invalid characters or an odd character count cause FormatException.

examples.title: Decode a protocol marker
examples.code:
var marker = Convert.FromHexString("4859504552");
Console.WriteLine(Encoding.ASCII.GetString(marker));
examples.explanation: Each character pair restores one byte, producing the ASCII text HYPER.

commands.name: SHA256.HashData
commands.description: Calculate a SHA-256 digest.
commands.definition: Computes the 256-bit SHA-2 digest of supplied bytes or a stream. A cryptographic hash detects changes but does not encrypt data or authenticate an unkeyed message.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The bytes or readable stream to hash.

examples.title: Hash text deterministically
examples.explanation: The same input bytes always produce the same 32-byte digest.

commands.name: HMACSHA256.HashData
commands.description: Calculate a keyed SHA-256 authentication code.
commands.definition: Computes an HMAC-SHA-256 value from a secret key and message. Unlike a plain hash, a valid HMAC demonstrates knowledge of the shared key.

examples.title: Authenticate an in-memory message
examples.explanation: The random key must be retained securely by any party that later verifies the message tag.

commands.name: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes
commands.description: Generate cryptographically strong random bytes.
commands.definition: Fills or returns bytes produced by the operating system's cryptographic random-number generator. It is appropriate for keys, salts, nonces, and security tokens.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: The number of random bytes to return.

examples.title: Create a random token
examples.explanation: Thirty-two unpredictable bytes are encoded for text-safe storage or transport.

commands.name: RandomNumberGenerator.GetInt32
commands.description: Generate an unbiased secure random integer in a range.
commands.definition: Returns a cryptographically strong integer at least as large as the inclusive lower bound and smaller than the exclusive upper bound without modulo bias.

examples.title: Choose a secure six-digit code
examples.code:
var code = RandomNumberGenerator.GetInt32(100000, 1000000);
Console.WriteLine(code);
examples.explanation: The exclusive upper bound keeps every result at exactly six decimal digits.

commands.name: CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals
commands.description: Compare secret byte sequences without early-exit timing.
commands.definition: Tests equal-length byte sequences using work that does not depend on where their first mismatch occurs, reducing timing leakage during tag or token verification.

examples.title: Verify an HMAC tag
examples.explanation: FixedTimeEquals is suitable for comparing authentication tags after their lengths and encodings are validated.

commands.name: Stopwatch.StartNew
commands.description: Start measuring elapsed time immediately.
commands.definition: Creates and starts a high-resolution Stopwatch using the best timing source available on the current platform.

examples.title: Measure an operation
examples.explanation: Elapsed time includes the asynchronous delay until Stop freezes the measurement.

commands.name: Stopwatch.GetElapsedTime
commands.description: Calculate elapsed time from Stopwatch timestamps.
commands.definition: Converts one or two raw Stopwatch timestamps into a TimeSpan using the current platform's high-resolution timer frequency.

examples.title: Measure without allocating a Stopwatch
examples.explanation: Raw timestamps provide a compact timing path for small measured regions.

commands.name: Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly
commands.description: Get metadata for the assembly containing the running code.
commands.definition: Returns the Assembly whose code is currently executing, enabling inspection of its name, version, attributes, resources, and defined types.

examples.title: Report the generated snippet assembly
examples.explanation: The Hypershell C# runner compiles snippets into a temporary HypershellSnippet assembly.

commands.name: Assembly.GetTypes
commands.description: Get every type defined in an assembly.
commands.definition: Returns Type objects for modules defined in the assembly. Type loading can fail partially when dependencies are missing, producing ReflectionTypeLoadException.

examples.title: List types declared by the snippet
examples.explanation: The generated Program type and any types declared in the snippet appear in the assembly metadata.

commands.name: Type.GetProperties
commands.description: Inspect properties exposed by a runtime type.
commands.definition: Returns PropertyInfo metadata matching the requested public/non-public, static/instance, and declared/inherited binding rules.

examples.title: List DateTime property types
examples.explanation: Reflection reports metadata rather than reading any particular DateTime instance.

commands.name: Type.GetMethods
commands.description: Inspect methods exposed by a runtime type.
commands.definition: Returns MethodInfo metadata for methods matching the requested binding rules, including overloads and inherited members.

examples.title: Find string methods with one parameter
examples.explanation: MethodInfo metadata can be filtered by signature before any method is invoked.

commands.name: Activator.CreateInstance
commands.description: Create an object from its runtime Type.
commands.definition: Invokes a matching constructor for a Type selected at runtime. The result is object-typed and may be null for Nullable<T>; constructor and accessibility errors can throw.

parameters.name: arguments
parameters.description: An object array containing constructor arguments.

examples.title: Construct a generic list dynamically
examples.explanation: The concrete List<string> type is formed and instantiated entirely from runtime metadata.

commands.name: RuntimeInformation.IsOSPlatform
commands.description: Test the current operating-system platform.
commands.definition: Compares the current runtime platform with a supplied OSPlatform value so platform-specific behavior can be guarded explicitly.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: An OSPlatform value such as OSPlatform.Windows.

examples.title: Choose a platform-specific path separator
examples.explanation: RuntimeInformation identifies the platform without parsing an operating-system description string.

commands.name: ArrayPool<T>.Rent
commands.description: Rent a reusable array of at least the requested length.
commands.definition: Obtains an array from a shared or custom pool to reduce repeated large-array allocation. The returned array may be longer than requested and must be returned exactly once.

examples.title: Use and return a temporary byte buffer
examples.explanation: The requested region is used and the array is returned in finally; clearing prevents residual bytes from being exposed to a later renter.

commands.name: ArrayPool<T>.Return
commands.description: Return a rented array to its pool.
commands.definition: Makes an array previously obtained from the same pool available for reuse. The caller must stop accessing the array after it is returned.

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: The exact rented array to return.

parameters.name: clearArray
parameters.description: Whether the pool should clear elements before reuse.

examples.title: Return a sensitive character buffer
examples.explanation: clearArray trades extra work for reducing the chance that a later renter observes old character data.

commands.name: Memory<T>.Slice
commands.description: Create a bounded memory view without copying elements.
commands.definition: Returns a Memory<T> view over part of the same underlying storage. Changes through either writable view affect the shared elements.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: The number of elements in the slice.

examples.title: Fill one region of an array
examples.explanation: The Memory<byte> view refers to indexes 4 through 7 of the original array without allocating another array.

commands.name: Enum.TryParse<TEnum>
commands.description: Try to parse an enum name or numeric value.
commands.definition: Attempts to convert text into a specified enum type without throwing for invalid text. An overload controls case sensitivity.
commands.template: var valid = Enum.TryParse<{enumType}>({text}, ignoreCase: true, out var value);

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The candidate enum name or number.

examples.title: Parse a day name case-insensitively
examples.explanation: The generic type fixes the allowed enum values while ignoreCase accepts lowercase input.

commands.name: BitConverter.GetBytes
commands.description: Convert a primitive value into machine-endian bytes.
commands.definition: Returns the in-memory byte representation of a supported primitive. The byte order follows the current architecture and should be normalized explicitly for portable protocols.

examples.title: Inspect an integer representation
examples.explanation: The output order depends on the architecture, which IsLittleEndian reports explicitly.

commands.name: GC.GetTotalAllocatedBytes
commands.description: Read the process-wide managed allocation counter.
commands.definition: Returns an estimate of the total bytes allocated by managed code since process start. It is a cumulative diagnostic counter, not the current live heap size.

parameters.name: precise
parameters.description: Whether to synchronize for a more precise value.

examples.title: Measure allocations around a small operation
examples.explanation: The difference includes managed allocations made by the measured code and relevant runtime activity.
